Hi all,

Thanks for sharing the redlines and the context, Logan. I reviewed BlueWave's proposed edits and drafted alternative language that I believe preserves BlueWave's privacy concerns while allowing Redwood the ability to reference the relationship for product credibility. Key recommendations below (I'll attach the tracked changes):

1) Publicity: Replace the proposed blanket prohibition with the following compromise clause:
   "Customer shall not issue press releases or public statements referring to Redwood Inference or use Redwood logos without prior written approval, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld and shall be provided within five (5) business days of the request. Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither party shall be prevented from making disclosures required by applicable law or regulation, provided the disclosing party gives the other prompt written notice and, to the extent practicable, cooperates to limit the disclosure."

Rationale: five business days gives a realistic review window for legal + marketing sign-off and is industry standard for enterprise launches. If BlueWave needs a shorter window for the initial launch, we can agree to a one-off exception documented in the Order Form.

2) Testimonials / Quotes: Proposed text: "Customer grants Redwood the right to request approval for a testimonial or quote; Customer shall provide approval or suggested edits within three (3) business days. If Customer does not respond within three (3) business days, approval will be deemed granted, unless Customer has previously notified Redwood of a specific blackout or embargo period."

Rationale: protects both parties and prevents indefinite hold-ups while giving the customer control.

3) Logo usage & assets: Add explicit reference to an asset pack and brand guidelines; require that public-facing logo usage adhere to the brand guidelines. Request that Customer provide high-res color and white-background SVG/PNG files.

4) Order Form language: Remove the "pre-approved reference" statement and instead add an Annex in the Order Form that lists approved use cases (e.g., press release, case study, logos) and the point of contact for approvals. This lets us handle the initial launch exception without changing the MSA.

I've attached a short redline_summary.xlsx that maps BlueWave's asks to our proposed edits. Logan — if BlueWave is comfortable with an initial 3-business-day exception for a single launch announcement (documented in the Order Form annex), we can accept that and keep the MSA language at 5 business days for the running relationship.

Lauren — once Sara confirms the asset types needed, can marketing prepare the packs?

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
